overview.text: The Redbelly Snake is a tiny, harmless woodland snake of Canada and the eastern United States, named for its bright red or orange belly.

identification.text: Orange, grey, black or brown on the back with a bright red or orange belly. Many have a light ring behind the head.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Southern Canada from Saskatchewan to Nova Scotia, and the eastern half of the United States.

habitat.text: Woodlands; it hides under logs and leaves. In the north it uses old ant mounds, which stay warm in the sun.

behaviour.text: A secretive snake. It may curl its lips, play dead, or puff itself up like a venomous snake to put off predators.

diet.text: Mostly slugs - its thin, curved teeth help it hold slimy prey.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young every year, about 7 to 9 at a time.

funfacts.text: It sometimes curls its upper lip when threatened - scientists are still working out why.
